what_we_tried: Tried reusing one LRAT core proof for sibling cubes.
why_it_looked_promising: Sibling cubes differ by one unit, so a proof might transfer.
how_it_was_killed: Measurement: 0/6 transferred. Backward closure used every unit of the original cube.

what_we_tried: Tried a second solver for timed-out leaf cubes.
why_it_looked_promising: Different solvers can solve different instances.
how_it_was_killed: The same 4 leaves timed out under both solvers.

what_we_tried: Tried proof-prefix lookahead in place of position cubes.
why_it_looked_promising: Proof prefixes might select better splits.
how_it_was_killed: It lost on all 3 tests and ran 1.9 to 2.5 times slower.

what_we_tried: Tried lowering the per-cube time limit.
Tried a proof-size cap to reduce CPU use.
why_it_looked_promising: Smaller proofs might reduce total work.
how_it_was_killed: Splitting raised CPU cost by a factor of 21. The cap remained useful for memory, parallel work and restartability.
evidence: On 126 p = 53 cubes, 6.3 CPU hours became 133.4 CPU hours, measured 2026-08-12.

why_it_looked_promising: A fixed shard seemed a simple deterministic assignment.
how_it_was_killed: Split children outside their assigned shard were lost; shuffled work order replaced it.

why_it_looked_promising: Parameter tuning might speed the refutations.
how_it_was_killed: The tested flag was already the default in version 4.0.4.

what_we_tried: Tried two simulated-annealing witness searches with repair moves.
why_it_looked_promising: Local search might find a witness near the known frontier.
how_it_was_killed: Neither variant passed p = 53 validation; both stalled.

what_we_tried: Used small local language models (about 4B parameters: a Qwen model and Phi-4) as generators of structural rules for the sets.
why_it_looked_promising: A cheap local model might suggest structures that restrict the witness search.
how_it_was_killed: Measurement: the rule proposed by the Qwen model was empty, since the Cauchy-Davenport theorem already gives |A + A| >= 2k - 1; the Phi-4 runs failed twice for technical reasons.
condition_to_revisit: Models of 27B parameters or more were not tested; that is a separate question.

what_we_tried: Tried a cube-difficulty predictor for scheduling.
how_it_was_killed: The maximum projected gain was below my adoption threshold.

what_we_tried: Considered a second version of the language-model search loop (branch ordering) with the mixture-of-experts model Qwen3.6 35B-A3B, as a successor to the first version, which worked on witnesses.
why_it_looked_promising: The model was downloaded and the branch-ordering component had been delivered and validated, so the second version looked like the next step.
how_it_was_killed: Operational: it was never connected. The same evening the exhaustive search closed a(18), a(19) and a(20), so the need disappeared.
evidence: Recorded 2026-08-08: model downloaded, loop still on version 1 (witnesses), version 2 not connected.
condition_to_revisit: Only if branch order, not proof size, became the bottleneck.

what_we_tried: Tried extending the earlier class-counting method to p = 59, k = 15.
why_it_looked_promising: It had counted p = 53 correctly: 182, 4.9 billion nodes, 9,892.6 seconds.
how_it_was_killed: The p = 59 run had no result after 21.5 hours.
evidence: Started 2026-08-27 14:59; still unfinished after 21.5 hours on 2026-08-28. Scope closed at 11 <= p <= 53.
condition_to_revisit: None for that method beyond p = 53.

what_we_tried: Tried clearing a first version of the prefix-hash cache.
why_it_looked_promising: Clearing entries seemed enough to avoid stale keys.
how_it_was_killed: It removed a second-depth entry and made an audit slow. A pinned clause object fixed the measured regression.
evidence: p = 59, k = 14 audit: 77 seconds before fix, 0.7 seconds after; 0 self-test mismatches and 300/300 comparisons.

what_we_tried: Computed the p = 73, k = 16 class list on a temporary worker.
how_it_was_killed: The completed output was erased with the worker. A previous output was lost the same way.
evidence: Up to 8 days and about 190 core hours lost; first output lost 2026-08-28 and erased 2026-09-08 12:27; second erased 2026-09-16 17:05.
condition_to_revisit: A durable, checked copy of the result.

what_we_tried: Considered a task-farming scheduler for the certificate workers.
why_it_looked_promising: It was a standard queueing tool for the machine.
how_it_was_killed: The run used a custom pool of 128 single-threaded workers per node instead; the proposed profile was not done.
evidence: 128 workers per node; no measured scheduler comparison.

why_it_looked_promising: They seemed capable of supplying the needed compute.
how_it_was_killed: None became the working certificate pipeline.
evidence: Operational options were rejected or not started during 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-11.

why_it_looked_promising: It appeared able to run the cube workload for weeks.
how_it_was_killed: The available allocation ended in 5 days; the workers did not have the assumed priority setting.
condition_to_revisit: A verified allocation and worker priority.

what_we_tried: Tried placing a batch script through a nested shell command.
how_it_was_killed: Double escaping left variables literal; the batch process exited immediately.

what_we_tried: Repeated the p = 73, k = 16 class-list computation after two lost outputs.
why_it_looked_promising: The method had produced an output twice; durable storage was the missing step.
how_it_was_killed: This retry succeeded and was checked independently.
evidence: Completed 2026-09-17 19:24: COUNT = 4, 34,804,379,608 nodes, 48,325.58 seconds. Four sets were checked 3 times, last on 2026-09-24; p = 71 regression COUNT = 2.
